account: It is just after ten on day 0, and I have reached the plaza for my scheduled market walk. I have not yet seen convincing evidence of anything unusual in town. Townsfolk 30, standing with Townsfolk 10 and 20, says there is no news. The secretary also reported no correspondence or news this morning. My appointment book lists ordinary mayoral business: the market walk, lunch at home, accounts at one, tea at an east-bank dockside cottage at three, office at four thirty, and home at seven. Tomorrow includes a mill grain inspection. One small uncertainty is the tea appointment: the book names only 'the neighbour,' and the secretary does not yet know the host's name. I asked for the name and exact cottage to be confirmed before three. The secretary initially asked which engagements to enter even though I had just read and returned the existing schedule; this may simply have been confusion, not evidence of a scheme. The secretary has now followed me toward the plaza carrying a writable book, but I do not know why, and I could not make out a remark made while I was walking away. My feeling that something is happening without me remains only a suspicion. So far, I cannot identify any hidden activity, its participants, or its purpose.
